topic: The Science of the Longevity Diet

text.content: Heavily reliant on processed meats and refined sugars, traditional Western diets account for millions of premature deaths globally every year. Formulating a statistical model to evaluate the benefits of altering these habits, Norwegian researcher Lars Fadnes projected that a shift toward plant-heavy nutrition could extend human lifespan by almost a decade. While his data suggests a 20-year-old achieves the maximum gain, an extension in life expectancy exceeding seven years can still be attained by a 60-year-old who permanently abandons Western foods.

Although theoretical models offer useful insights, empirical evidence is essential for demonstrating how daily food intake influences the aging process over time. Comprehensively analyzing the dietary choices of thousands of independent elderly people across parts of East Asia and Europe, Australian academic Zhaoli Dai-Keller gathered exactly this kind of real-world data. What emerged was a set of common characteristics: these long-lived individuals routinely selected varied diets rich in legumes and fish, while maintaining a sodium intake far below the population average.

To achieve advanced age without developing chronic medical conditions, consistent nutritional habits must be established much earlier in life. Following an extensive review of health records spanning several decades, evidence confirming that a Mediterranean-style eating pattern during mid-life is essential for preserving health into one's seventies was published by Harvard researchers Anne-Julie Tessier and Marta Guasch-Ferré. Conversely, healthy aging was rarely observed among participants whose mid-life consumption regularly featured foods high in saturated fat and salt.

In addition to the specific foods consumed, overall body mass exerts a nuanced effect on health during the aging process. Although a lean physique was recorded among most healthy centenarians, carrying a modest amount of excess weight may actually offer distinct advantages in later life. When assessing the capacity of older adults to perform basic daily activities independently, investigators observed that being slightly overweight provided greater support for routine physical function than remaining at a standard weight. By contrast, a 25 percent increase in the probability of severe physical impairment was recorded among underweight individuals.

Since lower body mass is frequently linked to increased longevity, severe calorie reduction is occasionally advocated as an intervention against biological aging. Under controlled laboratory conditions, reducing the standard caloric intake of an animal by 25 percent has consistently proven to extend its overall lifespan. Nevertheless, implementing such drastic dietary limitations in human populations presents immense practical challenges. Furthermore, whether the accompanying loss of physical strength counteracts any potential lifespan gains remains unconfirmed. Ultimately, adopting a balanced diet focused on plant foods continues to be the most realistic strategy.

stage_1_headings.instructions: Match the correct function or central theme to each paragraph. There are two extra distractor headings.

options.text: Estimating the years gained by modifying eating habits
Observational data from exceptionally long-lived communities
The critical role of mid-life nutrition for healthy aging
How body mass affects physical independence in later life
The practical challenges of extreme caloric restriction
The financial costs of treating diet-related cardiovascular diseases
Why regular exercise is more important than calorie counting

stage_2_scanning.instructions: Scan the text rapidly. Match the specific individual or entity to their corresponding description or action.

questions.prompt: Which researcher created a mathematical projection showing that dietary changes could add nearly a decade to human life?
Which experts proved that maintaining specific nutritional habits during middle age is vital for later cognitive and physical health?
Which academic investigated the real-world dietary selections of thousands of highly aged individuals in two different continents?

stage_3_logic.instructions: Are the following statements True, False, or Not Given according to the text?

questions.prompt: Adopting a plant-based diet at the age of 60 yields the exact same increase in life expectancy as doing so at age 20.
questions.explanation: Paragraph A states that an individual making the switch at age 20 achieves the maximum gain of almost a decade, whereas a 60-year-old gains exceeding seven years, proving the increase is not identical.

questions.prompt: In laboratory environments, increasing an animal's standard daily food consumption by a quarter has been shown to prolong its life.
questions.explanation: Paragraph E explicitly states the opposite: it is 'reducing the standard caloric intake of an animal by 25 percent' that has proven to extend overall lifespan.

questions.prompt: Centenarians in Zhaoli Dai-Keller's investigation who drank moderate amounts of wine lived significantly longer than those who abstained.
questions.explanation: Paragraph B outlines the dietary traits of the centenarians (legumes, fish, low sodium), but provides absolutely no information regarding their consumption of wine or alcohol.
